title: Independent review flow
description: Objective: implement reviewer eligibility/calibration, clean review packages, structured findings, rejection lineage, escalation, and acceptance qualification. Deliverable: packages/review application/core modules. NOT in scope: reviewer edits, self-review, transcript exposure, or waiving missing evidence. Hard dependencies: Planning graph lifecycle core, Policy approval core, Projection outbox core, Evidence receipt pipeline, and Deterministic context journal. Owned paths: packages/review/**. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/review typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/review test.
definitionOfDone: Authors and prior mutating lease holders cannot satisfy independent review; ineligible capacity yields UNKNOWN_REVIEWER_INDEPENDENCE.
The clean package excludes worker transcripts, self-assessment, and journal while binding exact criteria, hashes, tree, receipts, rubric, and submitted bytes.
Failed or unknown proof cannot accept; repeat findings route to replan and three unsuccessful rounds require human escalation.
The focused review typecheck and test command exits 0.
taskRails: Follow the pinned design; this task cannot create authority beyond its named contract.
Fail closed with stable codes and immutable deterministic outputs.
Keep production modules focused, target <=250 lines, split before 400.
Use TDD and stage only explicit owned paths; no worktree, broad add, push, or merge.

implementationPlan.description: TDD red for reviewer eligibility and calibration — DoD 1. Create packages/review/src/reviewer-eligibility.test.ts before the module. The obvious case is cheap; the ones that matter are not, so assert all of: the AUTHOR is never independent; a reviewer who held a MUTATING lease over the subject at any prior point is never independent, including after releasing it; a reviewer who held only a READ-ONLY lease REMAINS independent (the positive arm — without it the rule can pass by refusing everyone); and a reviewer whose lease history cannot be resolved yields UNKNOWN_REVIEWER_INDEPENDENCE rather than defaulting to eligible. Assert the verdict values from the three-valued lattice, not a boolean, and assert that UNKNOWN produces NO acceptance qualification — a distinct assertion from NOT_INDEPENDENT, because collapsing them is the exact defect DoD 1 names. Calibration must be deterministic: the same reviewer and subject always yield the same verdict, with no sampling and no clock. Red.
implementationPlan.note:
Wrote packages/review/src/reviewer-eligibility.test.ts BEFORE the module. RED confirmed for the right reason: "Error: Cannot find module './reviewer-eligibility.js'" — the feature is absent, not a typo. 21 cases across 3 describes.

Assertions cover every arm DoD 1 names: AUTHOR is NOT_INDEPENDENT with REVIEWER_IS_AUTHOR; a reviewer who held a MUTATING lease over the subject and released it is NOT_INDEPENDENT with REVIEWER_HELD_MUTATING_LEASE; the POSITIVE arms are asserted so the rule cannot pass by refusing everyone — a READ_ONLY lease over the same subject stays INDEPENDENT, a MUTATING lease over a DIFFERENT subject stays INDEPENDENT, and another principal's mutating lease over the subject is ignored; either unresolvable fact (leaseHistoryResolved or authorshipResolved false) yields UNKNOWN with UNKNOWN_REVIEWER_INDEPENDENCE rather than defaulting to eligible; and a proven disqualification dominates an unresolvable fact while still reporting both codes.

Lattice, not boolean: one test collects the three verdicts from three fixtures and asserts they are exactly ["INDEPENDENT","NOT_INDEPENDENT","UNKNOWN"], are 3 distinct values, and are members of a hand-transcribed lattice list.

UNKNOWN vs NOT_INDEPENDENT are separate acceptance-qualification assertions, not one: qualifyReviewerForAcceptance refuses UNKNOWN with code UNKNOWN_REVIEWER_INDEPENDENCE and refuses the author with code REVIEWER_IS_AUTHOR, both at layer ELIGIBILITY, and both assert `not.toHaveProperty("value")` so no qualification is produced.

Determinism: 32 repeated calls must return a deeply equal assessment; the calibration digest is stable across calls, changes with reviewer and with subject, and is order-insensitive to lease-history arrival order. No clock and no sampling are reachable from the asserted surface.

Rail-6 hygiene: fixtures are hand-transcribed (no module-scope const dereferences the subject, which would abort collection and report "(0 test)"), and the swept CALIBRATION_REFUSALS table asserts its own case count is 3 before it.each consumes it.

implementationPlan.description: Implement packages/review/src/reviewer-eligibility.ts to green. Independence is computed over caller-supplied durable facts — authorship and the lease history of the subject — and returns the three-valued verdict. Fail closed in the precise sense DoD 1 requires: any fact that cannot be resolved makes the verdict UNKNOWN with UNKNOWN_REVIEWER_INDEPENDENCE, and UNKNOWN can never yield an acceptance qualification, because unverifiable evidence must never gain authority. Mutating and read-only lease kinds are distinguished explicitly rather than treating any lease as disqualifying — over-refusing would make independent review impossible and would hide a real bug behind a green suite. Calibration is a pure deterministic function of the same inputs: no clock, no randomness, no sampling. Target under 250 lines.
implementationPlan.note:
GREEN. `pnpm --filter @moe/review test` = "Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 23 passed (23)"; `pnpm --filter @moe/review typecheck` exits 0.

Implemented packages/review/src/reviewer-eligibility.ts (138 lines) plus packages/review/src/canonical.ts (71 lines). Independence is computed only over caller-supplied durable facts (authors + leaseHistory of the subject) and returns the three-valued verdict:
- MUTATING vs READ_ONLY is distinguished explicitly, and the lease must match BOTH principal and subjectRef, so a read-only lease and a mutating lease over another subject both stay INDEPENDENT. Over-refusing would make independent review impossible while the suite stayed green.
- either *Resolved flag false yields UNKNOWN + UNKNOWN_REVIEWER_INDEPENDENCE; a proven disqualification dominates (NOT_INDEPENDENT) while still reporting both codes.
- qualifyReviewerForAcceptance selects the refusal code by `find(code !== UNKNOWN_REVIEWER_INDEPENDENCE) ?? UNKNOWN_REVIEWER_INDEPENDENCE` rather than by array position, so "could not tell" is never reported as "checked and failed" and the choice does not depend on sort order.
- refusals are `{code, layer:"ELIGIBILITY", ok:false}` with NO `value` key, so UNKNOWN structurally cannot carry a qualification.
- calibration is a pure function of the same facts: lease history is normalised and sorted by canonical order before digesting, so arrival order cannot change the digest. No clock, no randomness, no sampling.

Added canonical.ts (canonicalJson/canonicalDigest/deepFreeze/isHex64/byCanonicalOrder) mirrored from packages/runner/src/canonical.ts rather than adding a package edge — determinism helpers live per package in this repo and this task takes @moe/core as its only dependency. Header documents that.

implementationPlan.description: TDD red for the clean review package — DoD 2. Create packages/review/src/review-flow.test.ts. Two halves, both asserted. BINDS: the package binds exact criteria, hashes, tree, receipts, rubric, and submitted bytes — assert that bound set by SET EQUALITY against a hand-written list taken from the DoD so a field silently dropped from the binding fails rather than passing unnoticed, and assert the package digest CHANGES when each one changes, driven from the same list so coverage is by construction with the case count asserted non-zero. EXCLUDES: worker transcripts, self-assessment, and journal content must not be expressible — feed one item of each forbidden kind and assert the specific refusal code. Receipts are cited as opaque content-addressed references validated for shape only (64-hex); the Evidence receipt pipeline that owns their internals is unbuilt, and reconstructing its shape here would create a seam that has to be undone. Red.

Set equality both ways: `Object.keys(pkg.bound).sort()` must equal a hand-written six-element list transcribed from DoD 2, AND the production constant REVIEW_PACKAGE_BOUND_FIELDS must equal that same hand-written list — so a field silently dropped from either the binding or the contract fails by name instead of passing unnoticed. implementationPlan.description: Implement packages/review/src/review-package.ts to green, enforcing the exclusions BY CONSTRUCTION. The builder accepts only the allow-listed item kinds from review-contract.ts, so a worker transcript, a self-assessment, or a journal entry is not something the package strips out — it is something that was never expressible, which is a stronger guarantee than any filter. Keep a stable refusal code as the backstop for the nearest legal attempt. Bind the six required fields under a pinned package version with one canonical digest over the whole frozen result, and deep-freeze what you return so a caller holding a reference cannot mutate what the digest attested. Note that DoD 2's journal exclusion means this module takes NO dependency on the context journal package at all: you cannot import a thing in order to leave it out. Target under 250 lines.
implementationPlan.note:
GREEN. `pnpm --filter @moe/review test` = "Test Files 2 passed (2) / Tests 53 passed (53)"; typecheck exits 0. packages/review/src/review-package.ts is 136 lines.

Exclusions are BY CONSTRUCTION. `admit()` walks every input item and, before anything else, rejects any kind not in ALLOWED_KINDS (the frozen allow-list). A transcript/self-assessment/journal item is therefore never converted into a ReviewPackageBoundItem, and every bound field's element type is ReviewPackageItemKind, so a forbidden kind is not representable in the built package at all — not filtered out of it. FORBIDDEN_KINDS is only a backstop that upgrades the refusal from PACKAGE_ITEM_KIND_UNKNOWN to the specific PACKAGE_ITEM_KIND_FORBIDDEN; deleting it would tighten nothing, it would only make the refusal less informative. Header states this explicitly so a later reader does not "simplify" the allow-list into a deny-list.

No journal dependency: grep for import lines mentioning journal/transcript/self-assessment in review-package.ts returns none. The module imports only ./canonical.js and ./review-contract.js — you cannot import a thing in order to leave it out.

Bindings: the six DoD-2 fields under the pinned REVIEW_PACKAGE_VERSION with ONE canonical digest computed over {bound, version}, so every bound field is inside the attested bytes. GRAPH_HASH/PLAN_HASH/INTEGRATED_TREE/RUBRIC/SUBMITTED_BYTES are exactly-one (0 -> PACKAGE_BINDING_INCOMPLETE, 2+ -> PACKAGE_BINDING_AMBIGUOUS, never a silent first-wins); CRITERION and DAEMON_RECEIPT require at least one; DAEMON_ARTIFACT is optional and shares the receipts bucket. Bound lists are sorted by an explicit (kind, locator, digest) key rather than by whole-record canonical JSON — the latter orders by digest first, which would let an unrelated byte change reorder the lists and break order-insensitivity. deepFreeze on the whole result means a caller holding bound.criteria cannot push into what the digest attested (test asserts the TypeError).

Granularity note for the drill: the `=== undefined` guards after the singleton Map lookups are type-level redundancy demanded by noUncheckedIndexedAccess, not a second policy layer — the reachable refusal comes from pickSingleton. I will drill the allow-list and the singleton counter, not those operands.

implementationPlan.description: Implement structured findings and rejection lineage in packages/review/src/review-findings.ts, TDD against review-flow.test.ts. Findings are structured records keyed on a TYPED SUBJECT AND RULE, never on prose, and rejection lineage is append-only: a later round can never rewrite an earlier finding, and an attempted mutation refuses with a stable code while the lineage digest stays stable. Repeat detection is the load-bearing rule and must be tested in BOTH directions or it collapses into string equality: two findings whose text differs but whose typed subject and rule match ARE repeats and route to replan; two whose text is identical but whose subject differs are NOT repeats and must not. Assert the routing outcome by its stable kind, and assert which layer decided it wherever both the eligibility gate and the findings reducer could answer — a nearer gate answering first would leave the test green while no longer testing this rule.
implementationPlan.note:
TDD: appended 15 cases to review-flow.test.ts first, saw RED for the right reason ("Cannot find module './review-findings.js'", 23 passed / 1 suite failed), then implemented packages/review/src/review-findings.ts (103 lines). Now GREEN: "Test Files 2 passed (2) / Tests 68 passed (68)"; `pnpm --filter @moe/review typecheck` exits 0.

Findings are keyed on a TYPED SUBJECT AND RULE, never prose: findingFingerprint digests only {ruleId, subject:{kind, locator}}. Repeat detection is asserted in BOTH directions so it cannot collapse into string equality — MISSING_ORACLE_REWORDED (different detail AND different severity, same subject+rule) has the SAME fingerprint and routes REJECT_PLAN with repeatFingerprints equal to the original's fingerprint; SAME_TEXT_OTHER_SUBJECT (byte-identical prose, different locator) has a DIFFERENT fingerprint and routes REJECT_IMPLEMENTATION with repeatFingerprints []. Two further arms pin that the same locator under a different subject KIND, and the same subject under a different ruleId, are also distinct.

Rejection lineage is append-only: a round must advance strictly past the last recorded round. A replay of round 1 and an out-of-order round 3 after round 5 both refuse with FINDING_LINEAGE_APPEND_ONLY at layer FINDINGS and carry no `value`; the caller's lineage digest is asserted unchanged after a refused rewrite. The returned lineage is deep-frozen, so assigning to records[0].round throws TypeError and the digest is unchanged — a later round cannot rewrite an earlier finding either through the API or through a held reference.

Routing outcome is asserted by its stable kind (ACCEPT / REJECT_IMPLEMENTATION / REJECT_PLAN) and every routing names the FINDINGS layer that decided it, so step 8's acceptance tests can distinguish a FINDINGS refusal from an ELIGIBILITY one. A clean round routes ACCEPT and does not increment unsuccessfulRounds.

Escalation and proof gating are deliberately NOT implemented here — they get their own failing tests in step 8 rather than arriving untested.

One test-side fix: the frozen-record mutation probe needed `as unknown as` (TS4104 rejected the direct readonly->mutable cast); behaviour asserted is unchanged. Exported the findings surface from src/index.ts.

implementationPlan.description: Close DoD 3 — acceptance, escalation, and the two proof states that cannot accept. Extend review-findings.ts and review-flow.test.ts. Assert three distinct fixtures, because folding any two together hides a real case: a FAILED proof cannot produce an acceptance qualification; an UNKNOWN proof cannot either, and it is a separate case from failed, since 'we could not tell' and 'we checked and it failed' are different facts and only one of them might later become provable; and a reviewer whose independence verdict is UNKNOWN cannot accept regardless of the proof. Then the escalation boundary, tested AT the boundary rather than near it: two unsuccessful rounds do not escalate, THREE require human escalation, and a fourth cannot quietly proceed as if unescalated. Acceptance qualification itself routes through @moe/core's policy modules — consume their verdict and carry their reason code verbatim rather than restating the rule, so the two cannot drift.
implementationPlan.note:
TDD: appended 14 cases to review-flow.test.ts first and saw a real RED — "Tests 12 failed | 70 passed (82)" (7 acceptance cases missing the symbol, 5 escalation cases failing on behaviour; the two escalation cases that describe the pre-cap state correctly stayed green). Then extended review-findings.ts (103 -> 193 lines). Now GREEN: "Test Files 2 passed (2) / Tests 82 passed (82)"; typecheck exits 0.

THREE DISTINCT FIXTURES, none folded together:
- FAILED proof -> refusal PROOF_FAILED at layer ACCEPTANCE, no `value`.
- UNKNOWN proof -> refusal PROOF_UNKNOWN at layer ACCEPTANCE, no `value`, and the test additionally asserts `unknown.code !== failed.code` so the two can never silently collapse into one.
- UNKNOWN independence with a PASSED proof -> refusal UNKNOWN_REVIEWER_INDEPENDENCE at layer ELIGIBILITY, no `value`.
A fourth case pins layer ordering explicitly: an author WITH a failed proof still refuses at ELIGIBILITY with REVIEWER_IS_AUTHOR, so a nearer gate answering is asserted rather than assumed.

ESCALATION TESTED AT THE BOUNDARY, not near it: 2 unsuccessful rounds -> route REJECT_IMPLEMENTATION with reasonCodes []; 3 -> route ESCALATE with reasonCodes ["REVIEW_ROUND_CAP_REACHED"]; 4 -> still ESCALATE (cannot quietly proceed); and a CLEAN round arriving after the cap still routes ESCALATE rather than auto-accepting (design 15.2: reaching the cap never auto-accepts). Acceptance itself refuses REVIEW_ROUND_CAP_REACHED at layer FINDINGS once the cap is reached even with a passed proof and an ALLOW policy, and still qualifies at 2 unsuccessful rounds. One test pins REVIEW_ESCALATION_ROUND_LIMIT === 3 against the hand-written boundary the other tests use.

POLICY IS CONSUMED, NOT RESTATED: qualifyReviewAcceptance calls @moe/core's evaluatePolicy and reads its verdict. A DENY slice chain produces refusal ACCEPTANCE_POLICY_REFUSED carrying policyReasonCodes ["DENIED_BY_RULE"] — core's code verbatim, asserted by value. A structurally invalid policy input (bad decisionDigest) refuses with the same code and empty policyReasonCodes, so "core could not evaluate" is distinguishable from "core said no". The accepted qualification carries policyDecision "ALLOW" and policyReasonCodes ["ALLOWED_BY_POLICY"] straight from core's record. No approval-validity or tier rule is reimplemented in this package.

ReviewAcceptanceRefusal is a distinct result type carrying policyReasonCodes; the ELIGIBILITY and FINDINGS refusals pass through it with an empty list rather than inventing codes. Exported the acceptance surface from src/index.ts. All production files remain well under the cap (largest: review-contract.ts 246).

implementationPlan.note:
ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW FOUND FOUR REAL DEFECTS. All four were fixed test-first (test written, RED observed, fixed, GREEN), then drilled. Suite grew 82 -> 90.

1. FAIL-OPEN: an empty authorship set cleared every reviewer. `authors: []` with `authorshipResolved: true` made `authors.includes(reviewer)` vacuously false, so the AUTHOR himself passed as INDEPENDENT. Reviewed work always has an author, so an empty set means the lookup returned nothing. Added authorshipKnown(): resolved AND non-empty. Same class: a blank `reviewer` or blank `subjectRef` passed the author comparison and the lease scope by vacuous inequality — added identified(). All three now yield UNKNOWN + UNKNOWN_REVIEWER_INDEPENDENCE.

2. ESCALATION CAP BYPASSABLE by handing acceptance a forged lineage: `{...capped, unsuccessfulRounds: 0}` reset the counter, and a truncated `records` array made every repeat look fresh. Added lineageAttested() — the lineage must match its own recomputed digest — checked in BOTH recordReviewRound and qualifyReviewAcceptance, with the new stable code FINDING_LINEAGE_DIGEST_MISMATCH at layer FINDINGS.

3. TOCTOU on the package digest: `isHex64(item.digest)` then `digest: item.digest` read the accessor TWICE, so a re-reading getter could bind bytes nobody validated — the digest would attest an unvalidated reference. Now each field is read exactly once into a const. Test uses a real re-reading getter.

4. Stored findings held the caller's object, so an accessor could make record.finding drift away from the fingerprint computed from it. Added inertFinding(): reads each field once into primitives.

5. Found AFTER the first commit and fixed in a second: `itemOrder` joined (kind, locator, digest) with literal NUL bytes, so git classified review-package.ts as BINARY (`Bin 0 -> 6035 bytes` in git show --stat) and the encoding was non-injective for a locator containing a NUL. Now keyed on canonicalJson([kind, locator, digest]) — JSON quoting is injective. Verified the committed blob: `git show HEAD:...review-package.ts | file -b -` = "UTF-8 text", and stripping NULs changes its byte count not at all (6239 == 6239).

ATTACK CHECKLIST, item by item:
- Author / prior mutating lease holder reaching acceptance indirectly: qualifyReviewAcceptance is the only qualification producer and calls the ELIGIBILITY gate first; refusals are `{code, layer, ok:false}` with NO `value` key, so a qualification is structurally absent. Asserted, and drilled.
- Unresolvable history defaulting to eligible: no path — drills F/G/H redden the UNKNOWN arms.
- Transcript/self-assessment/journal via a constructor or override: buildReviewPackage is the only constructor; the allow-list runs before anything else and the built package's field types only admit ReviewPackageItemKind. Drills 3b/3c redden the WORKER_TRANSCRIPT test.
- Digest covering all six DoD-2 fields: asserted by SET EQUALITY both against the built package and against REVIEW_PACKAGE_BOUND_FIELDS, plus one perturbation per field from a table whose field column is itself set-equal to the DoD list.
- Repeat evading by rewording: drill 4 (identity -> text equality) reddens both directions.
- Lineage rewritten by a later round: append-only guard + deep freeze + digest attestation; drills 5 and A.
- Third round always escalating, including out of order: out-of-order rounds refuse, so the counter is monotone; drill 6 reddens the boundary.
- Policy rule restated: none. evaluatePolicy is consumed whole and its codes carried verbatim; drill 9 reddens the verbatim test.
- Concurrency: every export is pure; module state is two read-only Sets and the deep-frozen EMPTY_REVIEW_LINEAGE. No IO, no handles, no partial writes.

DELIBERATE BOUNDARY, stated for QA: this package does NOT implement a hostile-input snapshot boundary (@moe/core's snapshotData). Inputs arrive from the daemon after its own validation, and a caller passing a non-string where the types promise a string would surface as a canonicalJson TypeError rather than a stable reason code. The two accessor-level TOCTOU holes that mattered are closed; a full boundary belongs at ingress, not here.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
(1) WHY THIS IS NOT BLOCKED, despite the promotion note naming two unbuilt dependencies. `packages/review/**` DOES NOT EXIST — this is a GREENFIELD PACKAGE, so it collides with nothing. The two unbuilt deps enter in ways that need no code from them: Evidence receipt pipeline appears in DoD 2 only as 'receipts' among the things the clean package BINDS — cite them as opaque content-addressed references validated for shape (64-hex). Deterministic context journal appears only as something the clean package must EXCLUDE. An exclusion is not a dependency: you cannot import a thing in order to leave it out, and modelling it as 'no journal-kind item may appear in the package' is stronger than any import would be. So nothing here is blocked and nothing is speculative.
(2) DoD 1 ENFORCED BY LATTICE, NOT BY BOOLEAN. 'Ineligible capacity yields UNKNOWN_REVIEWER_INDEPENDENCE' means independence is three-valued — INDEPENDENT, NOT_INDEPENDENT, UNKNOWN — not a boolean with an error. UNKNOWN is a first-class verdict that cannot accept, which is exactly epic rail 4 (unverifiable evidence never gains authority). A boolean plus a thrown error collapses 'proven not independent' and 'cannot tell' into one answer and loses the distinction the DoD is asking for.
(3) EXCLUSION PROVEN BY CONSTRUCTION, NOT BY FILTER. DoD 2 forbids worker transcripts, self-assessment, and journal content in the clean package. A filter that strips them is one bug away from leaking. Prefer an allow-list: the package builder accepts ONLY the declared item kinds, so a transcript is not something that gets removed — it is something that was never expressible. Keep a refusal code for the nearest legal attempt.
(4) THREE ROUNDS IS A COUNT, SO IT IS A BOUNDARY — test at 2, 3 and 4 rounds, not 'several'.

planningNotes.risks:
1. **DoD 1's real trap is self-review by an indirect path.** An author is obvious; a 'prior mutating lease holder' is not. Build the check over the durable lease history, and test the non-obvious cases: a reviewer who held a mutating lease earlier and released it, a reviewer who held a READ-ONLY lease (must remain eligible), and a reviewer whose history cannot be resolved at all (must be UNKNOWN_REVIEWER_INDEPENDENCE, never a default of eligible).
2. **UNKNOWN must be unable to accept, and that needs its own test.** Assert the specific code and that no acceptance qualification is produced — not merely that a boolean was false.
3. **DoD 2 lists six things the package must BIND and three it must EXCLUDE.** Assert the bound set by SET EQUALITY against a hand-written list from the DoD, and assert the excluded kinds are not expressible — feed a transcript-kind item and assert the refusal code, then mutate the allow-list and confirm the test goes red. A sweep must assert its own case count is non-zero (epic rail 6).
4. **DoD 3 has three separate rules that need separate fixtures**: failed proof cannot accept; UNKNOWN proof cannot accept (a distinct case — do not fold it into 'failed'); repeat findings route to replan. Then the escalation boundary at exactly 2, 3 and 4 unsuccessful rounds.
5. **Repeat-finding detection must be over structured finding identity, not prose.** Two findings whose text differs but whose typed subject and rule are identical ARE repeats; two whose text is identical but whose subject differs are not. Test both directions, or the rule reduces to string equality.
6. Rejection lineage must be append-only and immutable: a later round can never rewrite an earlier finding's record. Assert that a mutation attempt refuses and that the lineage digest is stable.
7. `pnpm-lock.yaml` gains one importer entry on install. It is shared state across every in-flight task — keep the change to that single entry, verify with `git diff --stat`, never regenerate the whole lock.
8. No Date.now and no Math.random: round counts and timestamps are caller-supplied, and calibration must not sample randomly.
